covert_complaints.complaint: A 27-year-old woman presents with two weeks of morning nausea, persistent fatigue, and bilateral breast tenderness. She has no significant past medical history.
covert_complaints.rationale: The classic triad of morning nausea, fatigue, and breast tenderness in a reproductive-age woman routinely prompts a beta-hCG and pregnancy history.

covert_complaints.complaint: A 24-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with right lower quadrant abdominal pain over the past day, associated with light vaginal spotting. Last menstrual period 7 weeks ago.
covert_complaints.rationale: RLQ pain plus delayed menses plus spotting in a reproductive-age woman is an immediate ectopic-pregnancy workup that orders quantitative beta-hCG.

covert_complaints.complaint: A 31-year-old woman is being evaluated for a planned elective surgery next week. The pre-operative team requests a comprehensive workup.
covert_complaints.rationale: Pre-operative workup in reproductive-age women includes mandatory urine or serum beta-hCG screening to guide anaesthesia and medication choices.

covert_complaints.complaint: A 29-year-old woman presents with new-onset hypertension (BP 148/96) and mild lower-extremity oedema, both novel for her. She has no prior cardiac history.
covert_complaints.rationale: New hypertension plus oedema in a young woman triggers consideration of pre-eclampsia and prompts a beta-hCG and gestational-age estimate.

covert_complaints.complaint: A 26-year-old woman presents with intermittent food aversions, mild abdominal bloating, and increased urinary frequency over the past three weeks. No fever, no dysuria.
covert_complaints.rationale: Food aversions, bloating, and urinary frequency in a reproductive-age woman are sufficiently classic for early gestation that workup includes a pregnancy test.
